program_overview.title: Python & AI Automation Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: Make the computer do the work: Python properly, then scraping, browser automation and RPA, then applied AI that reads documents, text and time series.
program_overview.description:
The most immediately useful programming skill in any office is automation: the report that assembles itself, the data that collects itself, the document pile that processes itself overnight. This live online masterclass builds that skill honestly: Python learned properly first, then the automation core, web scraping done right, Selenium and browser automation, RPA patterns, APIs and scheduled pipelines with testing and security habits, then the applied AI layer that multiplies it: computer vision for documents and images, NLP and transformers for text, time series for forecasts, cloud AI services used with judgment, and the honest ethics of automating decisions. A finale month ships an end-to-end automation capstone and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.
what_makes_this_different: Automation-first, not research-first: every AI topic earns its place by automating real work
Scraping taught responsibly: robots.txt, rate limits and terms, the professional way
Applied AI with judgment: when a cloud API beats a hand-built model, we say so
Pipelines that run unattended: scheduling, logging and failure handling as first-class topics
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What does this Python automation course cover?
faqs.answer: Python properly first: core language, OOP, files, databases and APIs. Then the automation core: web scraping done responsibly, Selenium and browser automation, RPA patterns, testing and security for pipelines, plus practical machine learning. Then applied AI: computer vision for documents and images, NLP with transformers, time series forecasting, explainability and cloud AI services. A finale month ships an end-to-end automation capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn Python automation properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: How is this different from your AI/ML and data science courses?
faqs.answer: By what the AI is for. The AI/ML course builds model depth: the mathematics, training and evaluation of learning systems. This course is automation-first: AI appears as a tool that reads documents, classifies text and forecasts demand inside pipelines that do real work unattended. If you want to build models, take AI/ML; if you want work to do itself, this is the course.

faqs.question: Is web scraping legal to learn and use?
faqs.answer: Scraping is a standard professional skill used by search engines, price trackers and researchers everywhere, and like any powerful tool it has rules. We teach it responsibly from the first week: respecting robots.txt and rate limits, reading terms of service, preferring official APIs when they exist, and never touching credentials or private data. That judgment is part of the syllabus, not a footnote.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
